question: The eighty-one head addresses carry a canonical nine by nine grid, because the address formula splits into two pairs of ternary places. Is that grid magic? What family of squares is generated by affine maps of the grid into the addresses, how many of them are magic at orders three, five and nine, and does the standard construction lie in that family? Finally, when a permutation is reported to preserve none of the thirty-five pairs of a relation, is that an ordinary outcome or evidence of antagonism?
level: External exact finite arithmetic over Z_n, exhaustive enumeration of affine squares and exact rational arithmetic; every statement decided by exhaustion; no text and no corpus count imported
domain: The canonical nine by nine grid of the eighty-one head addresses; the affine family of squares of orders three, five and nine over Z_n with all shifts; the standard odd-order construction; a thirty-five pair relation among eighty-one elements; the class labelling of the grid; and a declared manifest model

manifest_model.comment: A declared model of two directory listings and one manifest. The manifest is the snapshot's listing; the directory listing carries the works inserted after the snapshot at arbitrary positions. Only the set difference between the two declared lists is computed.

quantifiers: All eighty-one cells of the canonical grid for the line sums and both diagonals
All coefficient quadruples and all shift pairs of orders three, five and nine for the entry-set equivalence and the magic count
Every admissible shift at three declared points for the constant-row verification
All thirty-five pairs of the declared relation for the preservation arithmetic
All nine rows and nine columns of both the canonical and the block class labellings
grammar: exact integer arithmetic modulo the order, with coprimality by the Euclidean algorithm
exhaustive enumeration of affine maps and direct verification of the magic conditions
declared finite models, checked by exhaustion
acceptance: The address formula splits into the first pair of ternary places times nine plus the second pair, so the canonical grid is forced and its entry at row r and column c is nine r plus c plus one

The canonical grid is not magic: its row sums are eighty-one r plus forty-five, its column sums are nine c plus three hundred thirty-three, and exactly one row, one column and both diagonals reach the magic constant of three hundred sixty-nine, four lines out of twenty

In the canonical grid the middle row is the nine consecutive values through the middle, the main diagonal is the progression one, eleven, ..., eighty-one and the other diagonal is nine, seventeen, ..., seventy-three, each summing to the magic constant
An affine square's entries are one to n squared exactly when its coefficient matrix is invertible modulo n, verified for every coefficient quadruple at orders three, five and nine
Whenever the two row coefficients are units the row sums are constant and equal to n n (n-1) / 2 + n (n-1) / 2 + n, which is the magic constant n (n squared plus one) / two

The number of affine magic squares is exactly eight at order three, matching the classical count, and one thousand four hundred seventy-two at order five and three thousand five hundred twenty-eight at order nine

The standard odd-order construction is magic, is a permutation, and is affine at every declared order with the same coefficient matrix, one one one two, differing only in its shifts and having the middle value at its centre

A uniform random permutation of the eighty-one heads preserves two hundred forty-five over six hundred forty-eight pairs of the declared relation in expectation, and therefore preserves none with probability at least four hundred three over six hundred forty-eight, so the reported zero is an ordinary outcome
The canonical class labelling has exactly one class per row and per column, the block labelling exactly three, and the incidence statistic separates them from the maximum of eighty-one

A manifest built from a snapshot rather than from the directory loses exactly the works inserted after the snapshot, and every statistic computed from the manifest is a function of the snapshot, so it is internally consistent and the loss is undetectable from it
protected: No classical text, edition, transcription, commentary, name table, symbol table, sequence or annotation is imported, and no corpus count from any external repository is imported or recomputed here
The counts used, including the thirty-five pairs, the observed zero, and the corpus sizes, are declared numbers in this contract; they are checked for arithmetic consistency and are not re-measured
No claim about what any classical figure or chapter means, and no claim that a magic square is or is not part of any tradition

No claim that the reported permutation exists as described beyond what the declared preservation count implies; the arithmetic shows that preserving nothing is ordinary and does not establish that the permutation is what the external record says it is

No claim that the affine family exhausts the magic squares of any order; at order three the count coincides with the classical count of all magic squares, which is recorded as a coincidence of that order and not as a theorem
No claim that the class labelling measured anywhere is the block labelling; the block labelling is declared and is used only to give the incidence statistic a second value
No claim about the engineering of any external pipeline; the manifest model is declared and its arithmetic is the whole content
No floating-point value enters any acceptance test
No native Rust witness, no claim promotion beyond bounded-external-experiment, no Seal, no library admission
residual: What is established is a set of exact statements about declared finite objects: that the address formula forces a nine by nine grid whose entry is nine r plus c plus one; that this grid is not magic while four of its twenty lines nonetheless reach the magic constant; that an affine square is a permutation exactly when its coefficient matrix is invertible and has constant rows whenever its row coefficients are units, which reproduces the magic constant as a formula; that the number of affine magic squares is eight, one thousand four hundred seventy-two and three thousand five hundred twenty-eight at orders three, five and nine, with the standard construction sharing one coefficient matrix across all three; that preserving none of thirty-five pairs is what a random permutation does at least three fifths of the time; that a class labelling has between nine and eighty-one line-class incidences; and that a manifest built from a snapshot is internally consistent and cannot show its own loss. Nothing here decides any question about a text or a tradition. In particular the affine family is not claimed to exhaust the magic squares of orders five or nine, and the order-three coincidence is not elevated to a theorem; the grid is a grid of addresses and no claim is made that anyone placed anything in it; the preservation arithmetic bounds a probability and does not describe the reported permutation; the class incidence statistic is computed on a declared block labelling and not on the reported one; and the manifest model is a model, not an audit of any pipeline. No source sequence, symbol or chapter text is reproduced.
